name: Snow Jasmine
description: Golden jasmine tea from Yuanjiang Valley, with a floral aroma, grape-like sweetness and gentle acidity.
blend: 92% cold-brewed jasmine tea; grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: A light lunch, a fruit dessert, or the first glass of an unhurried evening.
photoAlt: A glass of Chalu at the table
pairings: Steamed fish with ginger
A gentle, aromatic dish that leaves room for the jasmine to shine.
Fresh prawn rice-paper rolls
Fresh herbs and a light filling meet the tea’s delicate floral character.
Pear & almond tart
A softly fruity finish alongside the tea’s gentle sweetness.
tasting_copy: Begin with the aroma before taking a sip. Snow Jasmine is a good place to explore the lighter side of the collection: follow the floral note first, then look for the gentle fruit character described in the tasting notes above.

Try your first glass on its own, then take another sip with a lightly flavoured dish. A little fresh ginger or a few herbs can give you a different way into the tea. Keep sauces gentle for your first pairing so you can still notice what is happening in the glass.
occasion_copy: Pour it as guests arrive for lunch, or set it beside a plate of rice-paper rolls for an easy starter. If you are tasting several Chalu teas, begin here before moving on to a more toasted or structured expression.
serve_copy: Chill the bottle well and open the cork carefully. Pour a little into a wine glass or flute, leaving room to appreciate the aroma. Taste before adding any garnish, then try a sip alongside the first bite of your meal. Keep the bottle chilled between pours.

name: Hibiscus Noir
description: A caffeine-free hibiscus and camellia blend. Red-fruit aromas meet floral notes and a structured finish.
blend: 94% cold-brewed herbal tea (hibiscus, wild camellia, strawberry, raspberry); grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: A cheese board, good conversation, and an evening that stretches a little longer.
photoAlt: Chalu Hibiscus Noir served with food
pairings: Roast duck
Berry aromas and a structured finish make a lively partner for a richer plate.
Mushroom risotto
An earthy, savoury dish with a contrasting lift of red-fruit character.
A soft cheese board
Creamy textures meet fragrant berry notes—an easy pairing to share.
tasting_copy: Take a moment with the colour and aroma before your first sip. Hibiscus Noir invites a closer look at the fruit-led side of the collection, especially when you have a richer dish on the table.

Compare a small glass on its own with a sip after food. Try roast duck for one meal, then an earthy mushroom dish for another. The suggested pairings below are different ways to explore the same tea, rather than a fixed menu you need to follow.
occasion_copy: Bring it out for dinner with friends, or open a bottle when you lay out a cheese board. Serve a small first glass and let everyone choose a bite to try with it. It also makes an interesting side-by-side tasting with the lighter Snow Jasmine.
serve_copy: Serve well chilled in a wine glass or flute. Open the cork carefully and pour slowly, leaving space in the glass for the aroma. Start with a taste on its own, then return to the glass with something savoury from the table.

name: Volcano Oolong
description: Tengchong oolong, toasted and rested on Yunnan oak. Dry, nutty and mineral in character.
blend: 94% cold-brewed oolong tea; grape juice, Yunnan oak, natural acids and CO₂.
pairing: Bring it to a seafood supper, or take your time with a glass all on its own.
photoAlt: Chalu poured into a glass for serving
pairings: Grilled sea bass
A little char echoes the tea’s toasted character without overpowering the fish.
Roast chicken with herbs
Savoury, golden flavours sit naturally alongside the oolong’s nutty depth.
Roasted mushrooms
Earthy flavours make room for the tea’s warm oak and mineral character.
tasting_copy: Give the first sip a little time before taking the next. Volcano Oolong is the expression to explore when you are drawn to the savoury side of a meal. Use its toasted and mineral tasting notes as a guide, then describe the finish in your own words.

Try it with a simple grilled dish first. A lightly charred edge or a spoonful of roasted mushrooms offers a useful contrast to tasting the tea by itself. You can then explore a more elaborate plate once you know what you enjoy in the pairing.
occasion_copy: Set it beside roast chicken for a weekend lunch, or pour it with grilled fish at dinner. For a tasting evening, compare it with Snow Jasmine in separate glasses and notice where your attention goes in each one.
serve_copy: Chill well before serving and open the cork carefully. Use a wine glass or flute, then take a small sip before the food arrives. Return to it with a bite of something grilled or roasted, keeping the bottle chilled between glasses.

name: Untamed Rosé
description: White Pu’er, rose, berries, citrus and pepper. A dry rosé expression with a lively finish.
blend: The featured blend brings together white Pu’er, rose petals, berries, citrus and Yunnan black pepper. This is a blend overview; consult the bottle label for the complete ingredient declaration.
pairing: An open-air lunch, a fruit dessert, or a just-because toast with friends.
pairings: Salmon with lemon
Citrus notes bring a bright counterpoint to the richness of the fish.
Burrata & tomato salad
Fresh acidity and creamy cheese meet a dry, berry-led pour.
Strawberry tart
A fruit-forward match that echoes the tea’s summer-berry aromas.
tasting_copy: Begin with the aroma, then follow the finish after your first sip. Untamed Rosé brings several tasting cues to explore, so take a moment to notice which one stands out to you before looking back at the notes above.

Try it first with a fresh dish, such as tomato and burrata, then revisit the glass with a bite of fruit. Those two combinations give you different ways to explore the same pour. The suggested dishes below are an easy place to start your own comparison.
occasion_copy: Choose it for a lunch that carries on into the afternoon, or a table of smaller dishes passed around to share. Save a little to try with a strawberry tart at the end of the meal and see how your impression changes.
serve_copy: Serve well chilled in a wine glass or flute. Open the cork carefully and begin with a small pour so there is room to enjoy the aroma. Keep the bottle chilled as lunch unfolds and taste again alongside a fresh or fruity dish.
